subject: HIPAA BAA eligibility & PHI handling - follow-up

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-call recap and next steps (HIPAA / BAA eligibility)

Hi Sarah / Rajesh — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a clear path on HIPAA/BAA eligibility and PHI handling boundaries.

Summary from today's call:
- Redwood can sign a BAA for customers that put PHI on Dedicated or Private deployments (Dedicated GPU pools or our Private VPC / on-prem option).
- Our hosted multi-tenant API (standard Hosted) is not eligible for PHI by default; customers may only send de-identified data to Hosted.
- We are SOC 2 Type II in progress (testing window running); expected final attestation Q1 2030 — I’ll share the report as soon as it's available.
- Technical controls we’ll provide for Dedicated/Private: encryption at rest and in transit, KMS integration (customer-managed keys option), audit logs (per-request traces), and stricter network boundary controls.

Attachments I’m sharing here: Redwood standard BAA template and our vendor security questionnaire (attached as a questionnaire stub). Please review and share your preferred next steps.

Proposed next steps:
1) HealthCloud to start the vendor security questionnaire (attached). If you prefer, send your questionnaire and we’ll complete it.
2) Schedule a technical deep-dive (30–45m) with Dev to go over architecture, KMS options, logging, and PHI flow (suggest week of Dec 4).
3) Legal (Rajesh) to exchange BAA process — we can start from our template or review your standard BAA; either works.
4) I’ll follow up with SOC 2 timeline and a copy of our architecture overview.

Let me know if that aligns and any preferred dates for the technical call.

Best,

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@healthcloud.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-11-30T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap and next steps (HIPAA / BAA eligibility)

Hi Sarah — quick technical clarifications from the SE side: happy to dive deeper on a call but high-level answers below.

1) Hosted (multi-tenant) and PHI:
- Our hosted public API is operated on shared tenancy and we do not accept PHI on that tier; this is an organizational policy driven by shared infrastructure and audit scope.
- There are no hosted plans today that we recommend for PHI. If HealthCloud needs a fully managed option that will handle PHI, the correct fit is Redwood Dedicated (customer-dedicated GPU pools with VPC peering and private networking) or Redwood Private (customer-controlled VPC / on-prem).

2) Examples of PHI and eligibility on Dedicated/Private:
- PHI examples: patient full name + DOB + MRN, clinical notes containing identifiable info, patient identifiers in prompts, medical images where associated metadata can identify patients, call transcriptions tied to user IDs.
- On Dedicated/Private: PHI in request payloads is acceptable provided you configure network limits and key management per our engineering checklist. We support:
  - Customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own keys) for encryption at rest
  - TLS with mutual auth for in-transit
  - Per-request audit logging and retained traces (configurable retention)
  - Isolation of KV caches and no shared prefix cache for Dedicated deployments

3) Evidence and artifacts we can provide now:
- Our DR/backup and encryption architecture summary (attached).
- Current SOC 2 testing window in progress; we'll share a SOC 2 attestation as soon as complete.
- Network architecture diagrams and runbook for onboarding Dedicated customers.

I attached a short architecture overview that highlights the Dedicated/Private boundaries. Happy to walk through this on a call — I’m available Dec 4–6 afternoons PST.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.ai
